title: Part 91: General Operating Rules
description: Essential VFR/IFR flight rules, weather minimums, equipment requirements, and operating limitations every pilot must know

cards.back:
Visibility: 3 SM
Cloud Clearance: Clear of clouds

Memory aid: 'In Bravo, just see 3 and stay clear'

cards.front: VFR Weather Minimums - Class C, D, E (below 10,000')
cards.back:
Visibility: 3 SM
Cloud Clearance: 500' below, 1000' above, 2000' horizontal

Memory aid: '3-152' (3 miles, 1000 above, 500 below, 2000 horizontal)

Visibility: 5 SM
Cloud Clearance: 1000' below, 1000' above, 1 SM horizontal

Memory aid: '5-111' (5 miles, 1000 all around, 1 mile horizontal)

cards.front: VFR Weather Minimums - Class G Day (below 1200' AGL)
cards.back:
Visibility: 1 SM
Cloud Clearance: Clear of clouds

Lowest VFR minimums in the NAS!

cards.front: VFR Weather Minimums - Class G Night (below 1200' AGL)
cards.back:
Visibility: 3 SM
Cloud Clearance: 500' below, 1000' above, 2000' horizontal

Same as Class C/D/E below 10,000'

Visibility: 1 SM flight visibility
Cloud Clearance: Clear of clouds

Requirements:
• ATC clearance required
• At night: Pilot must be instrument rated, aircraft IFR-equipped
• Not available at all airports (see chart)

Maximum: 250 KIAS

Exceptions:
• ATC authorization
• Flight test operations

cards.front: Speed Limits - Within Class B or Below/Through Class B
cards.back:
Maximum: 200 KIAS

Applies:
• Below Class B shelf
• Through VFR corridor
• Within 4 NM of Class C/D primary airport at/below 2500' AGL

1000 feet above the highest obstacle within a horizontal radius of 2000 feet

Allows safe emergency landing if engine fails

500 feet above surface except:
• Cannot fly within 500 feet of any person, vessel, vehicle, or structure

Memory aid: '500/500 rule'

cards.front: Minimum Safe Altitudes - Open Water/Sparsely Populated
cards.back:
No closer than 500 feet to any person, vessel, vehicle, or structure

(Same as other than congested, no 500' AGL minimum)

Magnetic course 0°-179°: ODD thousands + 500
(3500, 5500, 7500, 9500...)

Magnetic course 180°-359°: EVEN thousands + 500
(4500, 6500, 8500...)

Memory aid: 'East is Odd, West is Even (EWOE) + 500'

Magnetic course 0°-179°: ODD thousands
(3000, 5000, 7000...)

Magnetic course 180°-359°: EVEN thousands
(4000, 6000, 8000...)

No +500 for IFR!

Enough fuel to:
• Fly to first point of intended landing
• PLUS 30 minutes reserve at normal cruise

Enough fuel to:
• Fly to first point of intended landing
• PLUS 45 minutes reserve at normal cruise

Memory aid: 'Night needs 45'

Enough fuel to:
• Complete flight to destination
• Fly to alternate (if required)
• PLUS 45 minutes at normal cruise

Always file REAL fuel endurance!

Alternate NOT required if destination weather:
• 1 hour before to 1 hour after ETA
• Ceiling at least 2000 feet
• Visibility at least 3 SM

Memory aid: '1-2-3: 1 hour window, 2000 ceiling, 3 SM vis'

A - Altimeter

A - Anti-collision lights

A - Altimeter (adjustable)

PLUS all VFR day/night equipment

Mode C transponder required:
• Class A (all)
• Class B (in and above)
• Class C (in and above)
• Within 30 NM of Class B primary airport to 10,000' MSL
• Above 10,000' MSL (except below 2500' AGL)
• Within ADIZ

Required in same airspace as Mode C transponder:
• Class A, B, C
• Within 30 NM of Class B primary
• Above 10,000' MSL
• Within ADIZ

Effective January 1, 2020

7500 - Hijack (Hi-Jack, 75)
7600 - Communications failure (Can't Communicate, 76)
7700 - Emergency (7 + 7 = 14, 2×7 = 14, lots of 7s = really bad)

Memory aid: '75 taken alive, 76 need a fix, 77 going to heaven'

1. Aircraft in distress (ALWAYS first)
2. Balloons
3. Gliders
4. Airships
5. Aircraft towing/refueling
6. Airplanes/rotorcraft

Memory aid: 'Balloons & Gliders Always (win)'

Aircraft on the RIGHT has right-of-way

The other aircraft must give way (usually by turning right or climbing/descending)

Both aircraft turn RIGHT

No matter who sees whom first

Aircraft being overtaken has right-of-way

Overtaking aircraft passes to the RIGHT

12,500' - 14,000' cabin altitude:
• Required after 30 minutes at altitude

Above 14,000' cabin altitude:
• Required continuously

Above 15,000' cabin altitude:
• Must be provided supplemental oxygen

Note: Pilots should offer oxygen earlier for passenger comfort

Required: Sunset to sunrise

Colors:
• Red - Left wing
• Green - Right wing
• White - Tail

Memory aid: 'Red-Right-Returning (maritime)'... wait, it's opposite! Left=Red, Right=Green

Required for ALL operations (day and night)

Exceptions: Safety reasons (such as during maintenance or when they might blind passengers during boarding)

Usually red rotating beacon and/or white strobes

Requirement: Must receive ATC CLEARANCE

'Cleared into Bravo' = you may enter
'Remain outside Bravo' = do not enter

Also need: Mode C, ADS-B Out

Requirement: Two-way radio communication ESTABLISHED

'Established' = ATC has said your callsign
'Standby' = NOT established!

Must have working radio and Mode C

ALL FLIGHTS:
• Become familiar with all available information

Away from vicinity of airport:
• Weather reports and forecasts
• Fuel requirements
• Alternatives if flight cannot be completed
• Runway lengths at intended airports
• Takeoff and landing distance data

The PIC is:
• Directly responsible for operation of aircraft
• Final authority as to operation of that aircraft

May deviate from ANY rule to meet an emergency!

If requested, must submit written report to FAA

PIC shall ensure each person is briefed on seatbelts and shoulder harnesses

Must be fastened:
• During takeoff and landing
• When directed by PIC

Children under 2: May be held by adult

Can fly if equipment is NOT required by:
1. Type certificate / Equipment list
2. 91.205 (VFR day/night, IFR)
3. Airworthiness Directive
4. Any other Part 91 rule

Must: Placard inoperative, deactivate or remove

Required on most U.S. civil aircraft

Exceptions:
• Training flights within 50 NM of departure
• Design/development flights
• Ferry flights to install/repair
• Agricultural operations
• Aerial advertising

Must be inspected within 12 calendar months

No person may operate in formation flight:
• Unless arranged with each PIC beforehand
• Never with passengers for hire

Aerobatics prohibited:
• Over congested areas or open-air assemblies
• Below 1500' AGL
• Less than 3 miles flight visibility
• Within Class B, C, D, E surface areas
• Federal airways
• Without parachutes (if carrying passengers)

Standard TPA: 1000' AGL

Larger/turbine aircraft: 1500' AGL

Always check Chart Supplement for non-standard TPAs!

Continue VFR, land as soon as practicable

Remember: Squawk 7600

Altitude: Highest of:
• Assigned
• Vectored
• Expected
• Filed (MEA)

Route: Continue on route cleared, then expected, then filed

18,000' MSL to FL600

IFR only
No VFR allowed
No Special VFR

IMMEDIATELY notify NTSB:
• Aircraft accident
• Listed serious incidents (91.271)

Within 10 days:
• Written report if accident

See Part 830 for details!
